audits.scope: Pass over main.tex (866 lines) + references.bib + macro.tex. Cross-checked manuscript claims against in-paper evidence (citations, internal references, experiments, proofs). Did not verify external sources beyond what the bibliography provides; the policy in AGENTS.md treats this audit as advisory, not as verified evidence.
audits.manuscript_state: Draft. Abstract empty (lines 57-59), Experiments section empty (lines 807-810), claim_scope.md and evidence_log.md still TODO placeholders. Several substantive claims already present in Introduction, Related Works, Method, and Security sections.
audits.summary: 16 findings recorded. The single largest claim-evidence gap is that the contribution claim of an empirical evaluation has no Experiments section behind it. There are also multiple missing citations for load-bearing primitives (Nystrom method, cc-Groth16, KZG), a soundness proof using undefined notation, and an internal contradiction with the paper's own description of zkVC.

open_findings.claim: We implemented a prototype of the proposed framework and evaluated its performance through benchmarks. The results demonstrate a significant reduction in prover costs for practical sequence lengths, showing that zkDietFormer is not only theoretically efficient but also practically deployable.
open_findings.evidence_found: Section 7 contains only a header and is otherwise empty.
open_findings.recommended_action: Either (a) remove the empirical-evaluation contribution from the Introduction until benchmarks exist, or (b) populate Section 7 with benchmark results before circulating the draft. Until then, the third contribution bullet is unsupported.

open_findings.evidence_expected: An abstract that states the problem, contribution, and headline result.
open_findings.recommended_action: Draft the abstract once Section 7 has at least one headline number; without it the abstract cannot honestly summarize the contribution.

open_findings.section: Section 1.1 Contributions vs. Section 2 Related Works
open_findings.claim: To the best of our knowledge, we present the first verification framework specifically designed for low-rank self-attention.
open_findings.evidence_expected: An explicit scope distinction from prior linear-constraint matrix-multiplication ZKP works (especially zkVC), and ideally a literature note in Related Works ruling out other low-rank-attention proof systems.
open_findings.evidence_found: Section 2 lines 132-134 itself describes zkVC as reducing matrix multiplication constraint complexity from O(n^3) to O(n). The closing paragraph (lines 137) lumps together prior O(n^2) works (Thaler/zkCNN/vCNN/zkML/zkMatrix) and zkLLM ("linear in theory but m is large") but does not address how the present work differs from zkVC's O(n) constraint claim.
open_findings.recommended_action: Add an explicit sentence in Section 2 distinguishing this work (low-rank self-attention with softmax) from zkVC (general matrix multiplication, no softmax/Nystrom). Defer the strict 'first' phrasing until a novelty-historian pass confirms no concurrent low-rank attention proof systems.

open_findings.claim: Nystromformer applies the Nystrom method~\cite{}--a technique widely used in matrix approximation--to reduce the computational complexity of the standard Transformer from O(n^2) to O(n).
open_findings.evidence_expected: A foundational reference for the Nystrom method (e.g., Williams & Seeger, NeurIPS 2000/2001).
open_findings.evidence_found: Empty \cite{} at line 188; references.bib has no entry for the Nystrom-method primitive (only Nystromformer the model).
open_findings.recommended_action: Add a Williams-Seeger-style entry to references.bib and fill in the \cite{} key.

open_findings.claim: Since zkDietFormer is built upon the cc-Groth16 protocol, it inherits its guarantees of completeness, soundness, and zero-knowledge.
open_findings.evidence_expected: A primary citation for Groth16 and for the commit-carrying / cc-Groth16 variant.
open_findings.evidence_found: references.bib has no Groth16 or cc-Groth16 entry. The Vectis entry (eprint 2024/1405) discusses CC-SNARKs but is not pinned to this specific claim.
open_findings.recommended_action: Cite Groth, EUROCRYPT 2016 ('On the Size of Pairing-Based Non-Interactive Arguments'), and the specific paper that defines the commit-carrying Groth16 variant being inherited from. The entire security argument hinges on this construction; leaving it uncited is the largest single security-claim gap.

open_findings.claim: the strong binding property of the KZG polynomial commitment ensures that the prover cannot claim values different from those already committed.
open_findings.evidence_expected: Citation to Kate, Zaverucha, Goldberg, ASIACRYPT 2010 ('Constant-Size Commitments to Polynomials and Their Applications').
open_findings.recommended_action: Add the KZG paper to references.bib and cite it at first use.

open_findings.claim: we leverage cp-link to additionally guarantee input consistency across these two computations.
open_findings.evidence_expected: An inline citation at the cp-link mention pointing to LegoSNARK (where cp-link is defined) or Lunar.
open_findings.evidence_found: LegoSNARK is cited earlier in Section 3.4, but the cp-link mention in Section 6 has no citation, so the reader cannot easily verify the claimed property.
open_findings.recommended_action: Add \cite{Legosnark} (or Lunar, depending on which definition is used) at the cp-link mention.

open_findings.claim: The soundness proof reasons over $\hat{D}^{-1}$, $\mathbf{\tilde F{A'}^+}$, $\mathbf{B}'$.
open_findings.evidence_expected: The proof variables should match the method-section variables ($\tilde F$, $\tilde A^+$, $\tilde B$), or the proof should explicitly define the primed/hatted versions.
open_findings.evidence_found: $\hat D$, $A'$, $B'$ are introduced without prior definition; the method section (lines 472-489) uses unprimed $\tilde F, \tilde A^+, \tilde B$ and never mentions $\hat D$.
open_findings.recommended_action: Rewrite the proof using the method-section notation, or insert a paragraph at the start of the proof that defines $\hat D$, $A'$, $B'$ in terms of $\tilde F, \tilde A^+, \tilde B$. As written, a reviewer cannot follow the proof.

open_findings.claim: When AB != C, the probability that a randomly chosen vector r satisfies (the Freivalds check) is bounded by O(1/|F|).
open_findings.evidence_expected: Either prove the O(1/|F|) field-size bound, or restate the soundness claim under the binary domain {0,1}^n with t-fold repetition.
open_findings.evidence_found: The text claims O(1/|F|), but the proof immediately restricts to r in {0,1}^n 'to simplify the analysis' and concludes epsilon <= (1/2)^t. The claimed and proven bounds are different.
open_findings.recommended_action: Pick one regime. If the protocol actually samples from F (as Section 4 line 400 suggests, r_n in F^n), prove the field-size bound. If it samples from {0,1}^n, change Section 4 and the soundness statement to reflect that and to require t repetitions.

open_findings.claim: the probability that a randomly chosen vector r satisfies ABx = C is extremely small
open_findings.evidence_expected: Variable name (r vs. x) should be consistent with Section 3.6 (Freivalds preliminary at lines 320-322), and the right-hand side should be Cr (not C).
open_findings.evidence_found: Mixes r and x; right-hand side reads 'ABx = C' rather than 'ABr = Cr'.
open_findings.recommended_action: Replace x with r and write 'ABr = Cr', matching Section 3.6.

open_findings.location: main.tex line 90 ('to O(n)') and line 371 ('size n + m^3 + n m^2 + m n d_v + m^3 + n m d_v')
open_findings.evidence_expected: An explicit statement of which symbols are treated as constants (m, d, d_v) and how m scales with n in the intended deployment.
open_findings.evidence_found: The expression on line 371 is O(n) only when m and d_v are treated as constants. The paper does not state this assumption. In the broader Nystrom literature m is often O(sqrt(n)) or O(log n), in which case the true cost is super-linear.
open_findings.recommended_action: Add one sentence clarifying that m, d, d_v are O(1) in n, or restate the headline complexity as O(n m^2 + n m d_v) so the dependence on m is visible. This is also a hook for the figure-table-audit pass once experiments exist.

open_findings.claim: Linformer ... can incur large mean squared errors compared to exact attention.
open_findings.evidence_expected: A citation to a paper that measures Linformer's MSE vs. exact attention (e.g., the Performer paper makes a similar critique).
open_findings.evidence_found: No citation attached to the MSE claim.
open_findings.recommended_action: Either cite the source of the MSE measurement or soften the wording to a structural critique (e.g., causal-masking incompatibility) that the cited Linformer paper itself acknowledges.

open_findings.claim: these approaches still require a prover computation complexity of O(n^2) ... ~\cite{Thaler, zkCNN, vCNN, zkML, zkMatrix}, or, even when achieving linear-time complexity in theory, suffer from the limitation that the other matrix dimension m remains prohibitively large in practice~\cite{zkLLM}.
open_findings.evidence_expected: The summary should account for zkVC, which the same section just described as achieving O(n) constraints.
open_findings.evidence_found: zkVC is omitted from both the O(n^2) bucket and the linear-but-m-large bucket. This leaves zkVC as a counterexample to the implicit 'no prior linear-constraint matrix-mul' framing that the contribution claim relies on.
open_findings.recommended_action: Either add zkVC to one of the two buckets with a specific reason it does not displace the contribution, or add a third bullet that names zkVC's limitation (no softmax handling, applies to general MM rather than self-attention).

open_findings.claim: this approach relies on implementations tied to specific TensorFlow versions.
open_findings.evidence_expected: Either a citation/source for this engineering critique of Sparse Transformer, or removal of the sentence.
open_findings.recommended_action: Drop the sentence; it is an implementation observation, not a methodological limitation, and Longformer's positioning in the narrative does not depend on it.

open_findings.claim: Ground-truth files for claim boundaries and numeric evidence
open_findings.evidence_expected: claim_scope.md should state the strongest claim, non-claims, and red lines (especially around 'first' and 'O(n)'). evidence_log.md should pin numeric claims (context-window numbers, Freivalds soundness bound, complexity expression terms) to sources.
open_findings.recommended_action: Before the next audit pass, fill claim_scope.md (especially the strongest claim and the red line around novelty/complexity wording) and evidence_log.md (the numeric context-window numbers, the soundness bound regime, and the m, d, d_v assumptions). Without these, future audits cannot anchor against an authoritative scope.

open_findings.claim: r_k is sampled from F^k (where k is the number of landmarks).
open_findings.evidence_expected: Avoid overloading k as both a Freivalds challenge dimension and an iteration index inside algorithms.
open_findings.evidence_found: k is also used as an iteration index in Algorithm 1 / Algorithm 2 (lines 504, 526-530).
open_findings.recommended_action: Optional rename of one of the uses; otherwise add a one-line note that k denotes the number of landmarks throughout.

open_findings.claim: BERT uses 512 tokens, GPT-3 uses a 2,048-token context window, ... 400K for GPT-5, and 10M for Llama 4 Scout.
open_findings.evidence_expected: All four numbers anchored in evidence_log.md with source URLs.
open_findings.evidence_found: BERT and GPT-3 numbers are well-known. GPT-5 (400K) and Llama 4 Scout (10M) are cited to OpenAI and Meta documentation pages dated 2025-12-31; both numbers should be re-checked against the cited URLs at audit time, since context-window figures vary by tier and have changed between announcements.
open_findings.recommended_action: When claim_scope.md / evidence_log.md is populated, copy the exact phrasing from the cited documentation pages into evidence_log.md; treat the numbers as pending verification until then.
